summary: Signal Keepers is a kid-friendly story game for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Players are astronaut Keepers who hop between three small planets (the Moon, Mars and deep space) and wake six sleeping NASA machines left behind: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Opportunity, InSight, Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10. To wake each machine, the player solves a diagnostics puzzle, then repairs it by choosing the right tool and fixing red problem spots. Once awake, the machine opens a world and tells its story in simple words, linking its mission to a real discovery, such as moonquakes, past water on Mars, the inside of Mars and interstellar space. Each machine gives a secret word that is used to decode a station radio message and travel to the next planet. Every fact card shows its NASA source. The game runs in any browser .
details:
Signal Keepers turns forgotten NASA hardware into friendly storytellers for children. The player is an astronaut who jumps between three small planets. On each planet two machines are asleep. The player chooses one, solves a diagnostics puzzle, then repairs it by picking the right tool (screwdriver, brush, multimeter, tweezers, soldering iron) and rubbing it on red problem spots until the ring fills. A wrong tool gives a friendly explanation of what the problem needs. When the machine wakes up, a portal opens into its own world. The player walks through the world while the machine tells its story in short, simple sentences, and can find hidden question marks that reveal verified facts with sources.

Benefits and impact: it helps school-age learners meet the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Opportunity, InSight, Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10 and understand the science they made possible: moonquakes and the layers of the Moon, past water on Mars, the inside of Mars, light-travel time and a message to the stars. Difficulty (easy, medium, hard) and challenge type (physics questions, deduction puzzles, decoding) adapt to the child. Keyboard, mouse and touch work, and reduced-motion is respected.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript only, with hand-built vector (SVG) artwork. No external libraries or media files. Sound effects are generated in the browser from noise (wind, whooshes, clicks); there is no music. An optional voice can read the story aloud.

Creativity and factors we considered: each machine has its own world as a metaphor for its story (a folded world, a Moon that rings like a bell, a 90-day clock, a journey to the core, distance as a world, a plaque to decode). Pictures are labelled "Artistic visualization", and waves are labelled "Illustrative reconstruction", never raw NASA data. Progress is saved only on the player's device. Layan Khmous created this project using an AI assistant, which helped write the code, story text and vector artwork.
